blocks.text: "At Home in the Universe": Accident or Inevitable Masterpiece?
When we try to create something new, we often feel like we are praying to the god of chance.
Are great ideas just accidental products falling from the sky?
Are hit products just lucky wins in the casino of the market?
Is our existence itself nothing more than a miraculous accident that happened by chance in the long history of the universe?
If so, creation is an incredibly lonely and unreliable activity.
However, Stuart Kauffman, a theoretical biologist at the Santa Fe Institute, counters this sense of emptiness head-on in his main book, titled At Home in the Universe.
He says the following.
"Life is not an improbable accident. It is an expected, inevitable result of the laws of physics and complexity."
Today, I will introduce Kauffman's philosophy of Self-organization, which gives courage to everyone involved in making things.
1. Darwin is Merely an Editor
For a long time in biology, Darwin's Natural Selection was considered the sole protagonist of evolution.
Random mutations occur, and those suited to the environment survive.
It was thought that repeating this for billions of years created the complex life we see today.
But Kauffman points out the following.
"Natural Selection is an excellent Editor, but not an Author."
Natural selection can trim away the bad from what already exists, but it has no power to create complex order from scratch in the first place.
So, who wrote the original draft of order?
The true author Kauffman proposes is Self-organization.
2. Order for Free
To make something complex, you need a complex blueprint.
We assume so.
But Kauffman proved a shocking fact using computer simulations called Boolean Networks.
Even with simple elements, if you connect enough of them, they do not become chaotic or disordered.
Instead, they spontaneously settle into stable, orderly patterns.
He called this Order for Free.
Just as oil droplets naturally form beautiful spheres in water, when a system becomes complex beyond a certain threshold, order arises on its own, even without a designer.
In other words, when you build an organization or run a community, you don't need to manage every detail rigidly.
As long as there are appropriate connections, order will come to you.
3. The Edge of Chaos is the Source of Creation
So, is it enough just to be complex?
Here appears Kauffman's most famous concept, The Edge of Chaos.
He divided the state of systems into three categories.
First is Order.
This corresponds to a solid state.
It is unchanging.
It is stable, but does not evolve.
Examples are rigid bureaucratic organizations or overly simple programs with no bugs.
Second is Chaos.
This corresponds to a gas state.
It changes too much.
It cannot hold past information, and accumulation is impossible.
Examples are collapsed projects or stormy upheavals.
Third is The Edge of Chaos.
This corresponds to a liquid state.
It is the boundary between order and chaos.
Kauffman argues that Life, intelligence, and evolution always exist at The Edge of Chaos.
It is a region stable enough to keep its shape, yet flexible enough to change its form according to the environment.
The best creative teams and long-loved products are always built on this precarious balance on the verge of collapse.
Too safe is no good.
Too free is no good.
Identifying this Edge is the greatest job of a leader or creator.
4. We are At Home in the Universe
The original title of the book, At Home in the Universe, contains a beautiful philosophy.
If life is just a random accident, we are intruders who wandered into a cold, indifferent universe.
But what if self-organization is a fundamental law of the universe, and order, or life, is necessarily born when complex things gather?
We are not an accident.
The universe expected beings like us to be born from the beginning.
We are beings who are At Home in this universe and allowed to relax.
Conclusion: Trust in Creation
Making things is not a lonely task of planting a flag alone in an empty wilderness.
It is an act of lending a hand to the huge flow of Self-organization that the universe originally possesses.
Do not fear the Edge of Chaos.
If you pour in enough passion and complexity, an inevitable masterpiece beyond your imagination will surely rise there.
